text:
mira: Heads up - EU2 dedicated pool-4 has been noisy since 09:10 UTC. p95->p99 jump on short-seq jobs (<=512). infra-bot flagged NIC drops on several rack-18 hosts.

sam: I saw the alert. any obvious tenant causing egress spikes?

devon: Quick look at the top talkers shows one tenant emitting a lot of small websocket bursts + frequent kv fetches. suspect egress microbursts.

anya: Can you paste the nic stats? curious if it's TX queue overflow vs driver interrupts.

devon: paste of ethtool and tc counters:
```
# ethtool -S eno1 | egrep "tx_|rx_|drop"
tx_packets: 18234567
tx_dropped: 1240
rx_packets: 17900123
rx_errors: 0
# tc -s qdisc show dev eno1
qdisc pfifo_fast 0: root refcnt 2 bands 3 priomap 
 backlog 0b limit 1000p requeues 2
```

sam: tx_dropped rising with requeues - sounds like kernel queue pressure not NIC hw. could be many small packets from the tenant saturating the host egress.

mira: We're seeing request latency correlate: short inference calls get 3x tail latency. Business impact on low-latency customers. Need quick mitigation and a longer-term plan.

infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1172. Detected host-level egress saturation on rack-18. Auto-mitigation suggestions: soft-evict noisy tenants, enable egress-rate-limit, or route to warm-pool.

anya: Quick mitigation plan (15-30m):
- soft-evict top 5 noisy allocs from pool-4 to warm-pool (no restart, just reassign)
- apply egress-headroom gating at node level: mark 20% headroom for dedicated slices
- enable per-tenant egress-quota for the suspected tenant at 200 Mbps

sam: Commands to soft-evict (allocator CLI):
```
# list noisy allocs
rictl allocs --pool=eu2-pool-4 --sort=egress --limit=10
# soft migrate
rictl migrate --alloc <alloc-id> --target warm-pool-eu2 --soft
```

devon: I ran list, top alloc is tenant:acme-ai (id a1b2c3). Migrated one instance as test. tx_dropped decreased on host-9 within 40s. latency improved ~30% on the test shard.

mira: Nice - can we roll this to the rest? any expected downstream cost/regressions?

anya: Two tradeoffs:
- warm-pool will increase consumed GPU-hours (roughly +0.5 GPU-hour per migrated alloc per hour).
- egress quotas might throttle legitimate high-throughput tenants (we should notify them).

sam: For long-term: propose "pin-by-egress-class" routing + headroom gating. Idea: classify tenants into egress classes (low/med/high). Low-latency short-seq tenants get egress-reserved lanes + KV cache affinity; high-throughput get egress-heavy slices. Router will prefer lanes based on class and current headroom.

devon: +1. Also add automated bump-down: if node NIC tx_drop > X for Y seconds, prefer routing new short-seq attempts to warm-pool or another AZ (if capacity). Fallback to model-quantized variant if cross-AZ latency acceptable.

mira: Sounds good. Can we capture expected cost delta for the egress-class carveouts? need numbers for product to approve.

anya: Rough estimate: carve out 2 dedicated egress lanes in EU2 (each 10Gbps logical) -> ~+3% infra cost for EU2 but reduces SLO breaches by estimated 60% for short-seq customers. I'll produce a short cost/report in the incident ticket.

infra-bot: Reminder: add postmortem tags if this escalates.

sam: For now I'll continue the soft-migrate rollout across pool-4 in 5m batches and monitor tx_dropped, p99 latency, and egress-metering.

mira: thanks - keep updates here, and ping me when we hit 50% of noisy allocs migrated. :thumbsup:

devon: Update 09:54 UTC: 6/10 noisy allocs migrated, global p95 latency down 22%, tx_dropped trending down.

mira: Good progress. We'll follow up on the pin-by-egress-class RFC after the incident.
